Leave-one-out validation and WAIC for GAMs

Source: R/loo.R, R/scam-methods.R
loo.gam.Rd

These methods evaluate the likelihood of each fitting observation at posterior coefficient draws and return the usual objects from loo. Neither method changes stats::logLik() for fitted GAMs.

Usage

loo.gam(
  x,
  ...,
  n_draws = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  sampling_args = list(),
  r_eff = NULL,
  chain_id = NULL,
  save_psis = FALSE,
  cores = 1
)

loo.bam(
  x,
  ...,
  n_draws = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  sampling_args = list(),
  r_eff = NULL,
  chain_id = NULL,
  save_psis = FALSE,
  cores = 1
)

waic.gam(x, ..., n_draws = NULL, seed = NULL, sampling_args = list())

waic.bam(x, ..., n_draws = NULL, seed = NULL, sampling_args = list())

loo.scam(x, ...)

waic.scam(x, ...)

Arguments

x

a GAM or BAM fitted by mgcv, or an independent-response SCAM fitted by scam.

...

additional arguments passed to loo::loo() or loo::waic().

n_draws

total posterior coefficient draws across all chains. Defaults to 4000 when generating draws; supplied draws determine their own count.

seed

random seed for posterior sampling.

sampling_args

named list of arguments passed to the coefficient sampler, including chains, diagnostics, method, mh_backend and method-specific controls; see log_lik().

r_eff

optional relative effective sample sizes, either one value or one per observation. Independent Gaussian draws use 1 by default. For Metropolis–Hastings draws this is estimated from the likelihoods. Supplied draws use their stored chain mapping when available; otherwise supply r_eff or chain_id.

chain_id

integer chain identifier for each coefficient draw, in draw order. Identifiers must be consecutive starting at one, and chains must contain equal numbers of draws. A supplied mapping must agree with the coefficient draws' stored mapping. Stored iterations determine temporal order for relative efficiency without reordering response or likelihood rows.

save_psis

retain the PSIS object in the returned LOO result.

cores

number of cores used by loo.

Value

A native loo or waic object, with attributes gratia describing posterior sampling assumptions and observation identifying fitting rows.

Details

The Gaussian posterior approximation and fitted values of additional family parameters are described in log_lik(). PSIS diagnostics assess the importance weights; they do not measure the accuracy of that approximation. With random-effect smooths, leaving out individual observations predicts further observations in the fitted groups, rather than new groups.

Likelihoods are evaluated one observation at a time using the function interface in loo. Saving PSIS weights still requires storage proportional to the number of observations times the number of draws.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("loo", quietly = TRUE)) {
  load_mgcv()
  m <- gam(mpg ~ s(wt, k = 5), data = mtcars, method = "REML")
  loo::loo(m, n_draws = 500, seed = 42)
}
#> 
#> Computed from 500 by 32 log-likelihood matrix.
#> 
#>          Estimate  SE
#> elpd_loo    -78.5 3.8
#> p_loo         2.9 0.8
#> looic       156.9 7.5
#> ------
#> MCSE of elpd_loo is 0.1.
#> MCSE and ESS estimates assume independent draws (r_eff=1).
#> 
#> All Pareto k estimates are good (k < 0.63).
#> See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
